comments.text:
This restriction on how many weapons the character can carry is one of the most idiotic and forced things I’ve ever seen, and it kills the fun. In GTA 4, RDR 2010, and GTA 5, you could carry all your weapons on your character, the difference being that in the original RDR, the weapons were visibly shown on the character’s back and in their holsters. In RDR2, you can only carry 4 weapons, and they are visible on the character, but the problem is that the horse’s saddle is some kind of magical portal that has 20 invisible weapons, and when you get close to it, you randomly pull weapons out of nowhere from the horse’s saddle.

Calling this realistic is way too forced, since there is nothing realistic about a horse’s saddle carrying over 20 invisible weapons that disappear and reappear out of nowhere. When you fall off or dismount the horse, long weapons also disappear from your inventory every time you select them while mounted, and then they vanish when you get off or fall off the horse.

Having this unrealistic and forced mechanic in GTA 6 makes no sense and breaks both logic and fun, because in GTA, you are constantly switching cars and means of transportation. If there is a magical trunk with 15 invisible weapons in the car, and you leave that car or it gets destroyed, you would lose access to your weapons. And in GTA, the car doesn’t come to you like it did in Cyberpunk 2077, so having all your weapons stored in the trunk of a car or in some vehicle storage system would not only remove the fun but also break the dynamic of combat and chaos that GTA has always had. You would have to constantly run back to your car just to change weapons. And running by pressing L3 instead of X is only useful for causing drift on a controller.

comments.text:
The End of the Arcade Era: The Rude Awakening in Vice City
​Anyone who shook their head and tossed Red Dead Redemption 2 aside back then because the pacing was "too slow" or the world "too realistic" should brace themselves for GTA 6. Rushing from mission to mission or blindly hurrying from one story point to the next won't get you anywhere here. It is no longer about mindlessly blasting through a campaign; it is about breathing in this world and living in it organically. This GTA will, in fact, be a game for professionals.
​The full force of this uncompromising life simulation will inevitably hit the pure arcade faction right in the face. The reality that many players rejected in 2018 is now striking back with full force—amplified by the raw power of a new console generation and deeply rooted in the unforgiving streets of a modern metropolis.
​Consequences as the New Foundation
​The days when you could magically wipe away wanted stars with a quick escape around the block or a fast respray are gone for good. GTA 6 demands a radical shift in mindset. Anyone who continues to treat Vice City as an undemanding sandbox for blind destruction will make their own digital survival a living hell. The game forces tactical discipline:
​The End of Anonymity: Crimes carry severe, long-term repercussions. The city does not forget your actions, and blind terror will inevitably lead to a gameplay dead end.
​The City as a Mirror: Your own appearance and demeanor must be constantly and deliberately maintained. One careless misstep leaves a lasting impact on how the entire environment and the NPCs react to you.
​Comprehensive Relationship Management: The dynamic between Jason and Lucia is just the absolute tip of the iceberg. It is about your constant interactions with the entire city, your networks, and your own reputation.
​Calculated Action: Every drawn weapon, every stolen car, and every escape route must be thought out in advance, instead of just acting on a whim.
​The Ultimate Gangster Manifesto
​This is simply no longer the GTA that the mainstream audience knows from the last decade. It is no longer enough to just have your eyes on the loot or the next kill. You have to actively control and shape the entire image you leave behind in this living world. Anyone who ignores these new rules of the game and continues to rely on pure chaos will be mercilessly crushed by the sheer immersion of this world.
